title: Crash in progress
caption: The merging galaxies Arp 256, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Arp 256 · constellation Cetus · about 350 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Two spiral galaxies with badly bent shapes fill this Hubble image, scattered with a huge number of blue star-forming knots that look a little like bursting fireworks. This is Arp 256, a system about 350 million light-years away in the constellation Cetus.

The pair is in an early stage of merging. As the two galaxies pass close to each other, their gravity pulls and twists them out of their original spiral forms, which is why their shapes are so distorted.

The blue knots are the most visible consequence. The close interaction between the galaxies has triggered a wave of star formation, compressing gas and setting off the birth of many new, hot stars that glow blue. Over time the two galaxies are expected to settle into one, but for now they are caught mid-collision.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.79 x 2.71 arcminutes) and distance (350 million light years), the frame spans roughly 284,000 × 276,000 light-years. Its light set out about 350 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image combines Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and Wide Field Camera 3, with filters in blue and near-infrared light and one tuned to glowing sulfur. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The near-infrared part of the data is invisible to the eye, and the pair is far too faint to see in this detail without a large telescope.

explore: The image, from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and Wide Field Camera 3, is a new version of one first released in 2008. That earlier image was part of a collection of 59 pictures of merging galaxies made for Hubble's 18th anniversary.
alt: Two distorted spiral galaxies scattered with many blue knots of star formation.
